title: python: add agent-orchestration templates and docs quickstart for multistep tool-calling
author: Maya Chen
description: Add a Python-focused quickstart and reusable templates demonstrating multistep agent orchestration and robust tool-calling patterns. Motivation: provide a compact, production-oriented example for developers building agents that call external tools (search, DB, calculators, web fetch) across multiple steps while preserving KV-cache usage, structured outputs, and graceful fallbacks. This PR introduces a written quickstart for the docs site, three templated agent implementations (stateless pipeline, stateful orchestrator with persistent context, and a notebook-driven interactive example), lightweight helper wrappers for common tools, CI smoke tests, and a small set of e2e scripts for local dev and CI. Highlights: - docs/quickstarts/agents-orchestration.md: step-by-step guide with configuration knobs (batching, timeout, fallback policy) and recommended metrics to track. - examples/python/agents/orchestration/templates/: modular code templates with typed interfaces, example tool wrappers for SERP, SQL, and runtime math, plus a sample policy file for routing and fallbacks. - examples/python/agents/orchestration/notebooks/stepwise.ipynb: interactive notebook demonstrating iterative prompt-state management and local KV cache visualization. - tests/examples/test_orchestration_smoke.py: fast smoke test that runs against the hosted dev model emulator; marked to skip in slow CI. - docs site nav entry and two small API doc snippets for the helper helpers. Implementation notes: templates are dependency-light and use the existing redwood SDK client; no new public API surfaces are introduced. The quickstart contains runnable commands for both Hosted API and Private deployments (VPC example). Related Linear: ENG-4981 (agent templates), ENG-5120 (docs quickstart), follow-up ENG-5250 (expand sample tool set). See test matrix and CI notes below. Merging strategy: squash merge after green CI and two approvals. Backwards compatibility: none required for existing examples; files are additive.
